facts.about: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd is engaged in the business of manufacturing, developing and marketing a wide range of branded and generic formulations and Active Pharma Ingredients (APIs). The company and its subsidiaries has various manufacturing facilities spread across the world with trading and other incidental and related activities extending to global market.  It is the largest pharmaceutical company in India.

flags.text: Cash-rich profits: 5-yr operating cash = 120% of PAT
Promoter stake down 1.8 pts in a year (now 52.68%)

business.summary: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd. is a global pharmaceutical company that develops, manufactures, and markets a wide range of pharmaceutical products, including generics, specialty medicines, and active pharmaceutical ingredients, to improve patient care across international markets.

segments.name: India
segments.note: Delivered strong performance driven by chronic therapies and deeper market reach.

segments.name: United States of America
segments.note: Revenue generated from pharmaceutical products including generics and specialty medicines.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.note: Delivered strong performance supported by innovative medicines and currency tailwinds.

segments.name: Rest of the world
segments.note: Focuses on disciplined execution and building stronger local market presence.

scorecard.promised: High single-digit consolidated top line growth for FY27.
scorecard.delivered: Delivering 11.2% year-on-year growth for the first half of FY27.
scorecard.evidence: Revenue grew 10.5% in Q1 FY27 and 11.9% in Q2 FY27, exceeding the high single-digit target.

scorecard.promised: R&D spend to be 6% to 7% of sales for FY27.
scorecard.delivered: Management expects a significant ramp up in H2 to meet this target.
scorecard.evidence: Current spending levels require a significant increase in subsequent quarters to reach the 6-7% annual guidance.

scorecard.promised: Expected to be in the range of 25% for FY27.
scorecard.delivered: Tax rate remains in flux pending the Organon acquisition closure.
scorecard.evidence: Management reiterated the 25% range guidance across multiple calls despite quarterly fluctuations.

scorecard.promised: Expect the acquisition to be completed in Q4 FY27.
scorecard.delivered: Integration management office is currently working on day-one preparedness.
scorecard.evidence: The horizon for completion is the final quarter of the current fiscal year.

narrative.scoreline: Management has consistently exceeded conservative revenue growth targets while maintaining a disciplined, practically debt-free balance sheet.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: India business growth is broad-based across therapy areas with robust performance.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Consolidated revenue grew 11.9% in the most recent quarter, supporting the claim of broad-based momentum.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Innovative Medicines crossed $1 billion in the US for the first time in FY26.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Annual revenue reached ₹58,462 crore in FY26, providing the scale to support a $1 billion specialty portfolio.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Margins improved due to a better product mix in branded and innovative medicines.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Operating margins rose from 27% in FY24 to 29% in FY25, though they dipped to 28% in FY26.

bull: Revenue growth of 11.9% in Q2 FY27 continues to outperform the high single-digit guidance.
Exceptional cash generation with 5-year operating cash flow reaching 120% of reported PAT.
Strong balance sheet with a 0.04x debt-to-equity ratio and ₹89,280 crore in net worth.
bear: Compliance issues at manufacturing sites continue to hinder new product approvals and generic business recovery.
Voluntary recall of 11 ophthalmology products and temporary cessation of manufacturing at the Assam plant.
Operating margins showed volatility, dropping to 27% in Q4 FY26 before recovering slightly.
watch: R&D ramp-up in H2 FY27 to meet the 6-7% of sales guidance.

claims.claim: Identified key things leading to slowdown, put interventions in place, and anticipate return to typical growth.
claims.quote: Yes, I don't want to get into the -- all the details, but we have identified a few key things that have led to the slowdown.

claims.claim: India business growth is broad-based across therapy areas with robust performance in prescription and volume.
claims.quote: What you said is right, the India business growth is across therapy areas.

claims.claim: Voluntarily recalled 11 ophthalmology products and initiated temporary cessation of manufacturing, keeping the regulator informed.
claims.quote: No, Vishal, I can't comment on what media has reported. But what I can say is that there are 11 ophthalmology products, which we have voluntarily recalled.

claims.claim: Growth is driven by field force expansion in tier 2 and tier 3 cities and new product launches.
claims.quote: We also -- you also know we did a field force expansion in the past, and that is also helping us to grow the business in tier 2, tier 3 tiers.

claims.claim: The decline is primarily due to Lenalidomide erosion and additional competition in certain products.
claims.quote: Our Innovative Medicines portfolio continued to grow, and this was offset by lower sales in the generic business, largely due to Lenalidomide erosion, but also due to additional competition in certain products.

claims.claim: Margins improved due to a better product mix, specifically growth in branded generics and innovative medicines.
claims.quote: We've seen good growth in our branded generics business as well as our innovative medicines business. Both of these have resulted in a healthier margin profile for the quarter.

claims.claim: Margins were lower due to lower milestone income, seasonality, reduced lenalidomide contribution, and elevated US spending.
claims.quote: Ex-forex, EBITDA margins were lower quarter-on-quarter due to several factors, including lower milestone income, some seasonality, reduced contribution from lenalidomide in Q4 versus Q3 and higher spend in certain geographies, including US.

claims.claim: Sun Pharma achieved its highest market share gain in India since the Ranbaxy acquisition.
claims.quote: I am pleased to note that this year, we have seen the highest gain in market share for Sun since Ranbaxy acquisition.

claims.claim: Innovative Medicines crossed $1 billion in the US for the first time in FY26.
claims.quote: I'm also pleased to note for the year that Innovative Medicines crossed $1 billion for the first time in the United States.

claims.claim: Compliance issues at manufacturing sites have hindered new product approvals and impacted top-line growth.
claims.quote: No, I think part of the question you answered yourself is that because of the compliance issue, we haven't been getting approval.

claims.claim: The generic business will recover once manufacturing compliance is achieved at sites to allow new product launches.
claims.quote: I think overall for the US, we see the innovative medicines continuing to grow and the generic business will start to recover once we are in manufacturing compliance for a number of our sites in order to launch new products.

claims.claim: Sun Pharma plans to launch generic Semaglutide in India on the day of patent expiry.
claims.quote: Sun Pharma plans to be in market on day-one of a generic launch.

claims.claim: The product is primarily targeted at new patients rather than those switching from existing therapies.
claims.quote: We would mostly anticipate new patients.

claims.claim: The company is open to raising debt for acquisitions if necessary to support long-term strategy.
claims.quote: At the same point of time, I think we have also indicated that for acquisition, if it is necessary, we are comfortable in raising debt.

risks.text: Company is involved in various legal proceedings including product liability, investigations, and regulatory matters.
Significant tax litigations exist, requiring management judgment on outcomes and deferred tax asset recoverability.
Related party transactions are essential to core business, requiring robust governance and arm's length verification.
Several manufacturing facilities are under regulatory scrutiny, including OAI classifications and import alerts.
